codeReviewIssues.description: The OpenTUI adapter test creates a mock UIActions object with 20+ no-op stubs manually inline. This is fragile — if UIActions gains a new method, this test will break at compile time but the fix is pure boilerplate. Consider extracting a createMockUIActions() helper into sprint-test-helpers.ts (similar to how mockExecutor/mockEvaluator are shared). Not blocking because the current pattern works and the test file is self-contained.

The ContextIndexer mock uses `as unknown as ContextIndexer & { capturedQueries: ContextQuery[] }` type assertion. This bypasses compile-time checking that the mock conforms to the full ContextIndexer interface. If ContextIndexer adds required methods in the future, this test won't catch the mismatch at compile time. Consider implementing all public methods of the ContextIndexer interface in the mock (startIndexing, getRelevantContext, dispose are already present, so this is mostly cosmetic).

summary: High-quality cross-area integration test file covering VAL-CROSS-004 (sprint event propagation to all 3 adapter types) and VAL-CROSS-006 (ContextIndexer integration with sprint loop). All 9 tests pass (46 expect() calls). The tests thoroughly cover: (1) Headless adapter log-level filtering across verbose/normal/minimal for all 6 sprint events, (2) OpenTUI adapter system block rendering with correct emoji prefixes via the real structured output pipeline, (3) MockAdapter event recording via exhaustive switch cases, (4) ContextIndexer query parameters (workflowType='sprint'), (5) context entry propagation into sprint phase prompt text, (6) Project Context section header rendering, and (7) absence of context section when no indexer is provided. The tests use proper DI patterns from sprint-test-helpers.ts, follow existing naming conventions, and run fast (<100ms). Worker followed the backend-worker skill procedure correctly. No blocking issues found.
